claim: k3s docs position embedded SQLite for 'a simple, short-lived cluster in your CI/CD environment' and embedded etcd for edge deployments that need HA without the overhead of managing a database; SQLite is the default and 'cannot be used on clusters with multiple servers'

k3s docs: an existing SQLite server converts to etcd by restarting with --cluster-init; once etcd files exist on disk the datastore arguments (--cluster-init, --server, --datastore-endpoint) are ignored; HA embedded etcd needs an odd number of servers and quorum is (n/2)+1; embedded etcd may have performance issues on SD cards

k3s etcd snapshots: scheduled snapshots on by default (00:00/12:00, keep 5 per server), configurable cron, compression and directory; optional replication to S3-compatible stores with its own retention (--etcd-s3-retention, default 5)
k3s ETCDSnapshotFile custom resources list all snapshots present on all cluster members through any Kubernetes client, unlike 'k3s etcd-snapshot list' which shows only the local node

kine README: 'Kine is not etcd'; an etcd shim implementing 'the subset of the etcd V3 API required by the Kubernetes API server - not intendend to be usable as a generic etcd server'; backends SQL (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres), Memory, NATS JetStream and T4; SQLite and Memory support only a single kine instance, HA needs external SQL, NATS or T4

kine's SQL log implements watch as a poll loop over the SQL table (1 s ticker plus a notify channel fed by local inserts) and re-creates etcd revision ordering: a revision gap is retried, and after more than 1 s a 'fill' record is written so watches do not stall
kube-apiserver --storage-backend: 'The storage backend for persistence. Options: etcd3 (default).'

etcd v3.6.0 (2025-05-15): average memory reduced by at least 50% (default --snapshot-count cut from 100,000 to 10,000, more frequent raft compaction), about 10% higher throughput, systematic robustness testing, and the first release with full downgrade support

etcd ran its robustness tests on the Antithesis simulation platform on 3-node and 1-node clusters with network faults, process kills, thread pauses, clock jitter and CPU throttling: 830 wall-clock hours simulating 4.5 years of use, across 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and main

etcd is governed as Kubernetes SIG etcd: OWNERS_ALIASES lists three chairs (ivanvc, jberkus, siyuanfoundation) and three tech leads (ahrtr, fuweid, serathius) with affiliations including Google and Broadcom
etcd released patches for three minor lines on 2026-10-22: v3.7.3, v3.6.16 and v3.5.35 (previous set v3.7.2/v3.6.15/v3.5.34 on 2026-09-22)

etcd v3.7.0 announcement (2026-07-08): RangeStream, keys-only range optimisation, removal of the last v2store remnants; coordinated adoption with Kubernetes 1.37 'possible thanks to the merger of etcd and Kubernetes development in 2023'

etcd hardware guide v3.6: fast disks are the most critical factor; slow disk writes can time out heartbeats and trigger elections; typically 50 sequential IOPS needed, 500 for heavy load; SSD recommended

etcd blog: upgrading v3.5.1-v3.5.19 directly to v3.6.0 may fail with 'membership: too many learner member in cluster'; users must first upgrade to v3.5.20+; two further upgrade issues were identified and fixed by 2025-10-21

k3s embedded etcd listens for clients on https loopback:2379 plus the node address:2379, and for peers on loopback:2380 plus node address:2380, whenever not in cluster reset; during --cluster-reset both bind to loopback only; metrics (2381) stay on loopback unless etcd-expose-metrics is set
Samsung 980 NVMe warranted endurance: 150 TBW (250 GB), 300 TBW (500 GB), 600 TBW (1 TB); warranty 5 years or TBW, whichever comes first
Olares sets K3S_DATASTORE_ENDPOINT (an external etcd) for k3s on master nodes, including single-box installs, and snapshots etcd every 30 minutes keeping 5 copies in /var/backups/kube_etcd

Olares issue #1716 (opened 2025-08-15, open): after fio showed very poor disk performance, an Olares maintainer advised against installing on an HDD 'because Olares relies on Kubernetes, which in turn depends on etcd, and etcd requires an SSD' (comment 2025-08-18)

Lab W5 idle-write window for etcd started at 01:19:14Z, the instant the in-place --cluster-init conversion finished (14.5 s) and the test pod (1 restart, ContainerCreating shortly before) reached Running; it counted the whole VM disk for 600 s: 340,568 sectors = 166 MiB (SQLite run: 39,008 sectors = 19 MiB); one run each

claim: k3s resource profiling (k3s v1.26.5, p95 of steady state, datastore and control plane only; x86 c6id.xlarge NVMe and Raspberry Pi 4 on UHS SD): disk requirement Kine/SQLite 10 IOPS, 500 KiB/s, <10 ms; embedded etcd 50 IOPS, 250 KiB/s, <5 ms; server RAM SQLite 1428-1596 M vs etcd 1450-1613 M (Pi 4 single-agent: 1215 vs 1413 M)

Derived: the lab's etcd idle rate (174,370,816 bytes per 600 s) extrapolates to about 25.1 GB/day and about 92 TB over 10 years (SQLite: about 2.9 GB/day, about 10.5 TB); against Samsung 980 ratings that is about 61% of 150 TBW, 31% of 300 TBW, 15% of 600 TBW; upper bound, confounded window (see -019)

k3s server sizing guide: 2 CPU/4 GB server supports 0-350 agents, 4/8 GB 351-900, 8/16 GB 901-1800, 16+/32 GB 1800+; a 3-server HA cluster scales roughly 50% more; join agents in batches of 50 or less

k3s resource profiling: operator-style apps that make extensive use of the datastore and creating many resources raise server requirements; agent and workload IOPS and workload storage should be isolated from the datastore, or the control plane may fail to maintain state
Kubernetes docs: each Node has a Lease in kube-node-lease and every kubelet heartbeat is an update request to that Lease object
k3s requirements page: TCP 2379-2380 between servers is 'Required only for HA with embedded etcd'; servers must reach each other on 2379/2380 only for HA
